description: qou-cds1: attacked through protium, the simplest beta decay (daughter 1H, so Q_beta = m_n - m(1H) exactly). With the corpus's derived scale E_0 = m_e/(q0(q0-1)), the counit of Delta_S prices 0.168 % from the ATOMIC target and 39.4 % from the nuclear one, so Delta_S already contains the emitted electron; building the element from protium's own NF instead is REFUTED (every required z is further from the derived cap than the corpus's). E_0*(-eps(Delta_S)) = Q_A identically (prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic), so the trace and ladder readings share their leading term BY CONSTRUCTION and the c_k are forced to be affine(z)/cos((z-1)h/2 - u/2) -- a reparametrisation residual, not an independent expansion. The 0.9985-vs-0.4991 z discrepancy is the 2508.65x slope ratio between the two correction functions. WITHDRAWS Step 15's claim that the functionals disagree and need a K off by 2.2656x: F_REQUIRED_TRM is exactly (Q_beta/Q_A)/affine(z_D). Lean: QOU/QBeta/DecayFunctionalUnification.lean, 5 theorems, sorry-free.

assertions.name: bridge_identity_E0_times_counit_equals_QA
assertions.detail: |E_0*(-eps) - Q_A| = 0.0 — prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic; Lean E0_mul_counit_eq_QA, generic over any char-0 field

assertions.name: corpus_decay_element_is_atomic_not_nuclear
assertions.detail: E_0*|eps(Delta_S)| is 0.1678 % from Q_beta = m_n - m(1H) and -39.41 % from m_n - m_p: a 234.9x discrimination, zero free parameters

assertions.name: protium_element_is_refuted_as_the_missing_factor
assertions.detail: on the physical pairing (atomic element, atomic target) the best z is 0.443947 from the derived cap, WORSE than the corpus's own 0.385812. One off-diagonal cell (atomic element vs the NUCLEAR target) is nearer at 0.338572, but that pairing is unphysical and is still 55 % of the way from z_D — so no cell rescues the route. The obvious move, and it double-counts the electron

assertions.name: two_functionals_share_their_leading_term_identically
assertions.detail: affine(1) = 1 and E_0*(-tr_M^1(Delta_S)) = Q_A exactly, so leading-order agreement is by construction and carries no information about which reading is right

assertions.name: z_discrepancy_is_the_slope_ratio_not_a_disagreement
assertions.detail: affine slope 1.11673 vs cosine slope 0.000445153 = 2508.65x; inverting each to the same measured correction gives z = 0.9985003044 and 0.4869951666

assertions.name: F_required_is_where_z_D_sits_on_the_affine_line
assertions.detail: (Q_beta/Q_A)/affine(z_D) = 1.75923699418 reproduces the committed F_REQUIRED_TRM to 3.64e-9 — WITHDRAWS Step 15's 'K off by 2.2656x, 20x outside the wall'

context.axis: qou-cds1: which decay functional is right — answered by dissolving it
context.answer: Neither is more right: they are one functional in two coordinates. The trace side is exact and affine in z; the ladder writes the same correction as cos(affine) times a power series, so the c_k are the coordinate-change residual. 'Re-derive the c_k ladder under D' has no hidden answer -- given z the ladder is defined by the equation. The live question is whether the cosine parametrisation should exist at all.
context.withdraws: Step 15 items 5 and its inference: the functionals do NOT disagree and do NOT need a K off by 2.2656x. F_REQUIRED_TRM is (Q_beta/Q_A)/affine(z_D).
context.scope: Scope-(a). Nothing derived, proposed, wired or readmitted; no convention adjudicated. The ladder-product figures at z_C and z_D show the parametrisation's behaviour and are NOT proposed c_k values. Delta_S closed forms are the corpus's, valid for the SHORT model.
